title: ReversibilityDistance
description: The published civic meter of the reidentification economy (reidentification-economy Appendix A). For a given release/twin it reports D, the reversibility distance: the residual identity entropy D = E[log2 k] in bits — how many bits of distinguishing information an adversary must still acquire to single a subject out of a population of N. D is measured against the singling-out budget budgetBits = log2 N; a release is fully reversed (reidentified) iff D == 0. The same number is the epsilon-unlinkability budget of a MultiversealTwin: privacy, capacity and reidentifiability are one ledger, not three knobs. Two orthogonal controls act on that ledger — a differential-privacy rate-limit that bounds how fast D may be spent per release, and a capture receipt that gates whether the identifying query Q is produced at all.

id.description: Stable URN for this reversibility-distance reading.

releaseRef.description: What release or twin projection this meter measures.

populationN.description: N — the population an adversary is singling out from.

budgetBits.description: The singling-out budget = log2(N). Total bits required to isolate one subject.

dBits.description: D — the reversibility distance = E[log2 k], the residual identity entropy: bits an adversary must still acquire to reidentify. D == 0 means the release is fully reversible.

reidentified.description: True iff dBits == 0 (the release singles subjects out with no residual budget left to spend).

unicityCurve.description: The unicity curve: for each number of observed points/joins p, the fraction epsilon_p of the population made unique.

epsilonP.description: Fraction of the population uniquely singled out after p points.

bitsPerPoint.description: Fitted log2(r): the per-point distinguishability, how many bits each additional observed point contributes.

pStar.description: Implied number of points/joins to reach k = 1 (full reidentification) = log_r(N).

method.description: The estimator that produced this reading.

name.description: Estimator name (e.g. the Appendix-A reversibility-distance estimator).

epsilonUnlinkabilityRef.description: Optional reference to the MultiversealTwin whose unlinkability.epsilon this D is the budget for. D IS that epsilon: one ledger governs privacy, capacity and reidentifiability.

controlPoints.description: The two orthogonal controls on the same ledger.

differentialPrivacy.description: How a DP mechanism rate-limits the change in D per release (e.g. 'rate-limits ΔD per release').

captureReceipt.description: How a capture receipt gates whether the identifying query Q is produced at all (e.g. 'gates whether Q is produced at all').
